Dürfen or Müssen? German A2 Permission and Necessity

Distinguish dürfen from müssen, including nicht dürfen and nicht müssen. Practise German permission and necessity with translations and explained answers.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Dürfen expresses permission; müssen expresses necessity or obligation. Their negated forms are especially important: nicht dürfen means not being allowed to, while nicht müssen means not needing to. English must not therefore normally corresponds to nicht dürfen, not to nicht müssen.

Common mistake to avoid

Du musst nicht kommen means you do not have to come. Du darfst nicht kommen means you are not allowed to come. Negation changes the practical meaning of the request.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Mit dieser Einladung darf ich den Saal betreten.With this invitation I am allowed to enter the hall.
Worked example 2Für den Kuchen müssen wir noch Eier kaufen.We still need to buy eggs for the cake.
Worked example 3Hier darf man während der Aufnahme nicht sprechen.People are not allowed to speak here during the recording.
Worked example 4Du musst morgen nicht mitkommen; es ist freiwillig.You do not have to come along tomorrow; it is optional.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose the correct present-tense form of dürfen or müssen for the stated permission or necessity. Keep the given nicht. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich ___ heute länger bleiben; die Gastgeberin erlaubt es. (permission)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: darf

Darf is the ich form of dürfen and expresses permission.

Question 2. Ich ___ die Aufgabe heute abgeben; die Frist endet. (necessity)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: muss

Muss expresses the stated deadline obligation.

Question 3. Du ___ hier nicht fotografieren; es ist verboten. (not allowed)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: darfst

Nicht dürfen expresses prohibition.

Question 4. Du ___ nicht teilnehmen; die Teilnahme ist freiwillig. (do not have to)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: musst

Nicht müssen removes necessity; it does not express a ban.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
